rationale: The sheet reads as a small set of repeated base types rather than a 20-option portfolio of materially distinct spatial families. Roughly 4 of the visible 10 are the same voided block chassis, and 3 more are closely related slab/notch variants. Only a few entries materially shift section or threshold language: the stepped lift family, the lifted bar family, and to a lesser extent the curved bent bar. That leaves the portfolio below the required diversity threshold and with one family clearly dominant. The program wants a compact street building with an active ground edge and one clear public void or terrace; several candidates satisfy that in principle, but the current set over-relies on box-dominated and repeated-footprint moves. The next graph should diversify macro-operators while retaining access-bounded ground thresholds and one readable public void per family.

repeated_family_groups.shared_language: block-based voided mass with front carve/open-court logic; same boxy chassis repeated with minor cut/cantilever variation
lifted or stepped mass with a similar bar/block sectional move and a calm upper cap; differences are mostly degree of setback/roof articulation
slab/prismatic frontage-notch masses with similar compact street-facing solids and shallow top manipulation

required_next_relations: Need 3+ new families built from different macro-operators: courtyard, carve_void, split_wing, bridge, cross_mass, bent_bar, puncture, cut_corner, terrace.
Preserve the required neighborhood contract by making the west street edge clearly inhabited and accessible in every kept family, not just carved.
Introduce at least one family where the void is through-running or corner-linked, not only front-notched.
Add at least one family with a true split-wing or cross-mass section so the portfolio is not dominated by box/bar chassis.
Keep upper mass calm, but vary the way the public space is formed: undercroft, court, terrace, notch, or lifted threshold should each have a different spatial logic.
Replace repeated block/court variants with masses that change footprint topology, not just roof profile or minor setback.
